props.title: Roma Ransom
props.face: Folk tunes, covers and originals, as a duo.
props.lede: There’s something about a violin and a guitar together that makes an event feel a little more special. Roma Ransom is Grace Easley on violin and vocals and Gordon Lewis on guitar, a married duo from Colorado Springs who play gypsy jazz, Romanian and Eastern European folk tunes and old-time ballads. They’re a lovely choice for a wedding or a dinner party.
props.headingNote: Here’s how booking through Signet works.

props.title: Roma Ransom playing their song Smoke Rings
Press and stages
props.pressTitle: In the press and on air

props.html: Grace and Gordon met busking on a street in Springfield, Missouri, and they’ve played together ever since. They named the duo for the music of Romania, and their song list runs from swing tunes like Caravan to Romanian and Eastern European folk, old-time ballads and their own songs. Both trained classically from an early age, Grace on violin and viola and Gordon on guitar, and Grace sings, too.

For about a decade they’ve played more than 200 shows a year, touring all over North America, and they’ve shared festival bills with Leftover Salmon and Larry and His Flask. Closer to home, they’ve played Dazzle in Denver and the Lon Chaney Theater in Colorado Springs, and they played a VIP event at the Pikes Peak Center for an Itzhak Perlman performance.

Their music has been in films and ads for Patagonia, Yeti, Huckberry and Bud Light, and Colorado Public Radio has featured them on Air Check. They bring their own sound system, so they can play outdoors or in just about anywhere you’d like them.

props.title: Configuration
props.note: Send us your date and we’ll help you plan the music around your event. They can play instrumental tunes or songs with vocals, or a mix of both.

rows.text: Book them for your ceremony, and a few swing and folk tunes give your cocktail hour a romantic, old-world feel.
They’re a great fit for a birthday, an anniversary or a dinner at home, when you’d like music with some character that still lets everyone talk.
Two classically trained players with a song list from Romania to Appalachia make a memorable dinner for clients or a team, at a volume where nobody has to raise their voice.
They bring their own sound system and play outdoors all the time, so a patio or a garden party is an easy fit.

props.html: Planning toasts or a program? We can work the music around them with your run of show. You can also get a general idea of what live music costs in Colorado from our cost guide.

props.html: Still have a question? Our full question list may have the answer.

items.q: Do they play instrumental music or songs?
items.a: Both. Much of their song list is instrumental violin and guitar tunes, and Grace sings the ballads and blues. We can plan the mix with you.
Yes. They’re both classically trained, and violin and guitar make a lovely ceremony. Let us know if you have a processional song in mind.

items.q: Do they bring their own sound?
items.a: Yes, they bring their own sound system. Just let us know how big the space is and whether you’re indoors or out.

items.q: Do they play outside Colorado Springs?
items.a: Yes. They play all over Colorado, from Denver and Fort Collins to the mountains. Tell us where your event is and we’ll let you know what’s possible.
